summary: A buried service crosses a boundary between two asset registers. Each register is complete for its own side and neither has a field for a member whose extent leaves it, so the crossing does not appear as a gap in either -- there is no row for it to be missing from.

signal_basis.figure_without_clock: searched: no figure governs the crossing
signal_basis.designed_control: searched: no control was proposed for it
signal_basis.no_instrument: the exclusion is in the schema. Neither register can hold a member that leaves its own boundary, so the absence predates the first reading
signal_basis.held_data_unasked: searched: no party holds data on a crossing neither register can represent

authoring_note: Built with a DELIBERATELY MISAIMED remedy: a training change addresses a routing failure, and the bin that fired is a schema exclusion. This is the case S0.2 exists for.

gap.why: Neither register's schema can hold a member whose extent leaves its own boundary. The medium cannot carry the shape, so the crossing has no row to be missing from -- which is why it does not read as a gap in either record.
gap.contested: BUDGET_BOUNDARY is the near neighbour: each register is a closed accounting compared to an open one. Recorded rather than resolved; the register's own UNI_003 says the mechanisms are not exclusive and filing is a choice.
